result:
Solutions 1 and 3 give answers that are provably too small, and Solution 2's answer of 3 is too small by the same argument. I did not determine the true value of n₀, only that it exceeds 8.

**Counterexample on 7 vertices.** Take the seven 4-sets that are complements of the lines of the Fano plane. Any two of them meet in exactly 2 vertices, so no triple lies in two of these 4-sets. Cover every triple not inside one of them with a 3-edge.

- Every 5-subset of the 7 vertices is the complement of a pair. That pair lies in some Fano line, and the complement of that line is a 4-edge B inside the 5-subset.
- In a 5-cycle on this 5-subset, exactly two of the five cyclic triples avoid the vertex outside B. Both of those triples lie in B, and B is their only covering edge.
- So the two triples need distinct hyperedges but only B is available, and no Berge-C₅³ exists on these 7 vertices.

Hence n₀ > 7.

**Counterexample on 8 vertices.** In the Steiner system S(3,4,8) there are 14 blocks, any two meeting in 0 or 2 vertices. Each block lies in 4 of the 56 five-subsets, and no 5-subset contains two blocks. So 14·4 = 56 five-subsets are covered exactly once, which means every 5-subset contains a block. The same argument rules out a Berge-C₅³, so n₀ > 8.

Therefore n₀ ≥ 9, and the answers 7, 6 and 3 are all incorrect.

VERDICT 1: REJECT
VERDICT 2: REJECT
VERDICT 3: REJECT
